title: One iOS standard for every iOS repo
why: Your reframe, Oct 27: "i never intended for the way i use these repos' interaction with ios/phone etc to be different ... i'm assuming there's best practices from each."
note: Plan (iOS kit consultation, report https://claude.ai/artifact/36CtFQ6CaTszMaxxZvuCXq, gold-standard column): one "iOS apps" page in claude-settings sets the standard for every iOS repo: the same make targets (phone, testflight, native-check); logic in an in-repo Swift package; XcodeGen; Swift 6; CI pinned to macos-26 that runs package tests and compiles every app; slow tests once per batch on the Mac through the shared simulator tool (c89); tokens.json generated into Swift; and your Oct 22 ruling "Mac install first, TestFlight fallback, every app" (recorded only in mailaudit). compliance-check flags drift. You plan more iOS apps, so it adds a new-app starter that sets up project.yml, the make targets, a Kit package, the CI workflow and an ios-ship entry. Known drift: home-app CI on macos-latest; ios-adblock in Swift 5.0 mode (6 files). Part 1, claude-settings (page, starter, compliance rows), needs no answer. Deferred (shiv, Oct 27): (a) the repo visits wait on your plan check; (b) one install rule for all iOS repos, timing per your answer (pick offered: a nightly Mac job about 3 AM CDT installs each app whose main moved; or the merging session installs when on the Mac; or only on request). Both are on decision cards in the iOS consultation thread. Port: yes, every iOS repo, new ones included. Placed ahead of c54, after c47 and c89 (triage, Oct 27).
